subject: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO / KMS / logging retention
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@fintechco.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@fintechco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO / KMS / logging retention

Hi Alice / Rajiv 

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- SSO: SAML 2.0 identity provider (Okta) with SCIM provisioning to sync groups.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys required; preference for AWS KMS with CMKs stored in their account. Potential need for HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) for certain data at rest.
- Logging/retention: Audit and request logs need to be retained for 13 months for compliance.
- Network: Some workloads will require network isolation / no public egress from inference nodes.

Open questions (would love confirmation):
1) SSO: is SAML mandatory for all users or only for admins? Any requirement for enforced IdP-initiated flows vs SP-initiated?
2) KMS: must the CMKs be in your AWS account (yes/no)? Any requirement for HSM attestation or FIPS 140-2 level?
3) Logging: Is 13 months the hard floor or can we retain logs externally (e.g., push to your SIEM) and keep shorter retention in Redwood?

Why this matters:
- Hosted API generally cannot support customer-owned KMS keys or private network isolation.
- Dedicated can support isolated capacity and private networking, but customer-managed KMS in the customer's account and HSM-backed keys typically require additional network connectivity and an integration pattern we should validate.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) is the safest option for CMK + long retention + strict network isolation, but involves longer lead time and enterprise contract terms.

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm answers to the three questions above?
- I'll loop in our SE (Vivek) for a follow-up technical deep-dive once you confirm.
- I attached a short requirements template to capture the specifics (FinTechCo_requirements_template.xlsx).

Thanks  looking forward to locking the recommended deployment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Attachment: FinTechCo_requirements_template.xlsx

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@fintechco.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO / KMS / logging retention

Thanks Marissa  quick answers from our side: 

1) SSO: SAML is mandatory for all users. We use Okta and will require SP-initiated flows for some admin tooling but IdP-initiated for most end-user access is fine. SCIM provisioning is preferred.
2) KMS: Yes, CMKs must be in our AWS account. For high-sensitivity data we require HSM-backed keys (we use AWS CloudHSM for certain regulatory workloads).
3) Logging: 13 months is a hard requirement for audit; we can push logs to our SIEM (Splunk) but Redwood must retain at least 180 days as buffer.

Also copying our security mailbox for any evidence requests: security@fintechco.com

Question for Redwood: would Dedicated with VPC peering and customer KMS (in our account) meet our requirements, or would we need the Private deployment? Curious on tradeoffs and lead times.

Rajiv
Director of Infrastructure, FinTechCo
rajiv.singh@fintechco.com

From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@fintechco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, security@fintechco.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO / KMS / logging retention

Thanks both  a few clarifications from product/security side: 
- Network: For our customer-facing inference (PCI-adjacent) we cannot allow public egress from inference nodes. VPC peering or PrivateLink is required.
- KMS/HSM: CloudHSM-backed keys are preferred for the most sensitive models; for everything else AWS KMS CMKs in our account are acceptable.
- Ops: We will need role-based access control mapping from Okta groups to Redwood roles.

If Dedicated can support VPC peering + KMS in our account + 13-month log forwarding/retention, we might accept that as a faster path. If not, we should plan for Private (VPC/on-prem).

Can Vivek or a SE confirm the technical feasibility and any additional compliance steps? Also, can you share your SSO integration guide and the KMS integration doc?

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Head of Product Security, FinTechCo
alice.turner@fintechco.com

Thanks Rajiv / Alice  appreciate the clarity. Summary and recommended path: 

Confirmed requirements:
- SAML (Okta) for all users + SCIM provisioning for groups.
- Customer-managed CMKs in FinTechCo AWS account; CloudHSM-backed keys for highest-sensitivity workloads.
- 13-month audit retention; Redwood to retain minimum 180 days and forward full logs to your SIEM for 13-month retention.
- Network isolation: VPC peering or equivalent required (no public egress for inference nodes).

Recommendation: Given the combination of CMKs in your account + CloudHSM + 13-month retention + strict network isolation, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the lowest-friction way to meet all controls with minimal custom engineering. 

That said, Dedicated with private networking + KMS-in-customer-account is a possible faster path if we can confirm technical feasibility from SE and sign an addendum covering key custody and logging retention. Dedicated will require:
- A technical implementation to mount KMS calls from our dedicated nodes to your account (cross-account IAM role + secure connectivity).
- Contract addendum for customer key custody and extended log retention SLAs.
- Potential SOC2 scope update for the Dedicated cluster if required by your audit team.

Next steps:
1) Vivek (cc'd)  can you confirm whether our Dedicated pattern supports CloudHSM-backed CMKs and VPC peering today, or whether that needs an engineering/workaround?
2) If SE confirms Dedicated can be made to work, I'll put together a short decision matrix and the required contract addenda for legal review.
3) Otherwise we'll scope Private deployment timelines (typically 8-12 weeks) and surface the procurement path.

I've attached our SSO integration guide and KMS integration doc for your team to review (redwood_sso_guide.pdf). Also linking the HubSpot deal for internal tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FT-2026-0421

Propose a technical deep-dive week of Jun 22  here's a 30-min slot to pick: https://cal.com/marissa/30min?date=2026-06-23

Thanks  I'll wait for Vivek's feasibility check.

Best,
Marissa Cole
